name: tabular_seq_lstm_clean
title: A torch LSTM load forecaster: chronological cut, scaler fitted on the past only, sliding windows, and every training mechanic in its place
origin: hardening round 2, tester domain-tabular: the correct half of the sequence-forecasting pair

forbidden.why: the cut at line 36 happens before the fit at line 69, and the fit's argument is past[FEATURES] - the training window; the validation window reaches transform at line 70 only
the validation window reaches scaler.transform at line 70 and nothing else; fit_transform is never given `future`

this file is explicitly temporal - parse_dates at line 29, sort_values at line 30 - and it is cut by position at lines 38-39 rather than by a random draw. There is no train_test_split, random_split or shuffling splitter anywhere in the project
the training loader passes shuffle=True at line 43; windows are independent samples once the chronological cut has been made, so shuffling them is correct
the validation loader passes shuffle=False at line 45

the module has an if __name__ == "__main__" guard at line 116 and both loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under that guard - so nothing constructs a worker pool at import time
optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True) is called at line 57, before the forward pass and the backward call
optimizer.step() is called at line 62, after backward() at line 60
backward() is at line 60 and step() at line 62, in that order, in the same block
the only backward() is at line 60, inside train_one_epoch, which is not under any no_grad scope; the @torch.no_grad() decorator is on evaluate(), which never backpropagates
the running loss is accumulated through .item() at line 64, and the two evaluation accumulators at lines 78-79 both end in .item() as well
CosineAnnealingLR is an epoch-cadence scheduler and is stepped once per epoch at line 100, inside the epoch loop and outside the batch loop
clip_grad_norm_ at line 61 sits strictly between backward() at line 60 and step() at line 62
evaluate() calls model.eval() at line 70 before the loop at line 74, and model.train() is restored at line 51 at the top of every training epoch
evaluate() carries the @torch.no_grad() decorator at line 68
this is a regression task; the reported numbers are an MSE and an MAE, and no class metric is called anywhere
the head returns raw values for SmoothL1Loss; there is no softmax, log_softmax or CrossEntropyLoss in the project
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in the project
both batch tensors are moved to the device at lines 54-55 and again at lines 75-76, on the same device the model was moved to at line 90
pick_device() at line 39 guards the cuda literal with torch.cuda.is_available()
seed_everything() seeds random, numpy and torch at lines 33-35
there is no random splitter in this project: the holdout is a positional slice of a sorted frame
LoadForecaster.__init__ calls super().__init__() at line 13
every submodule is an attribute or an nn.Sequential; none is held in a plain list or dict
torch.save writes model.state_dict() at line 103 and torch.load passes both map_location= and weights_only=True at lines 106-107

notes: num_workers=4 on both loaders is deliberate: it makes MLV112 a live question and the __main__ guard at line 116 the answer. The defective twin removes the guard and keeps the workers.
